newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Three S.Africans seriously ill with Congo fever.
newsitem.headline: Three S.Africans seriously ill with Congo fever.

text.p: South African doctors have contained an outbreak of deadly Congo fever at an ostrich abattoir but three workers are still seriously ill, a hospital spokesman said on Wednesday.

Abdul Rahman, chief medical superintendent of Tygerberg Hospital where 16 abattoir workers were being treated for the tick-borne disease in isolation wards, told reporters most would be discharged soon.
"Three of them are still actively bleeding, but all the other patients are in stable condition," he said.
One woman died of the disease in the eastern Cape town of Oudtshoorn, site of the abattoir, last weekend.

"We can safely say the situation is under control and we have contained the fever," Rahman said. "This is not an airborne disease... there's no need to panic or for unneccesary worry or anxiety by the public."
Congo fever, like the more notorious Ebola disease, causes body organs to degenerate with massive internal as well as some external bleeding. About 30 percent of Congo fever cases are fatal.

Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom said on Tuesday slaughtering had been halted to protect the 350 abattoir workers. Researchers believe the outbreak could have been caused by infected ticks jumping from their ostrich hosts onto workers.

The abattoir is run by the Little Karoo Cooperative, which controls about 80 percent of the world market in ostrich meat, hides and feathers. The cooperative has halted ostrich meat exports until further notice.

"As far as meat consumption is concerned there is no danger," Rahman said. "If an ostrich is infected and its meat kept in cold storage for more than 12 hours, the virus automatically dies; moreover if the meat is cooked it also dies."
